sections.html:
Franklin is the county seat of Johnson County, about 20 miles south of Indianapolis and 90 miles north of Louisville, Kentucky. It sits on Interstate 65 and U.S. 31.

Johnson County covers about 322 square miles and had 161,765 residents in 2020. Greenwood is the largest city in the county, and Camp Atterbury, a military installation, lies at the south end. Wikipedia names Franklin, Needham and Pleasant among the townships around the city, and notes that Needham, Franklin and Union townships merged in January 2022.

With about 26,743 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, Franklin is a small city next to a very large one.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Franklin's houses?
sections.html:
Franklin was platted in 1823 and named for Benjamin Franklin. Its post office opened in 1824, and the town was incorporated as a city in 1861.

Franklin College, a four-year liberal arts school founded in 1834, was the first college in Indiana to admit women. In the early 1920s the high school basketball team known as the Wonder Five won three straight state titles, from 1920 to 1922. The city's historic districts include the Franklin Commercial Historic District and the Martin Place Historic District.

sections.h2: What happened in the 2008 Franklin flood, and does it still matter?
sections.html:
In June 2008, Canary Creek, Hurricane Creek and related waterways overflowed, and more than 100 houses were damaged or destroyed. Some entire neighborhoods were affected.

The city and county then bought out flooded properties. An Indianapolis Business Journal report in 2013 said 107 homes would have been razed once the last six came down, using about $8.5 million in federal money. A 2014 report on one neighborhood described about 70 small homes destroyed by several feet of water, with the land since reforested by volunteers who planned 4,000 to 4,500 trees. The parks department maintains the site.

Flood maps were also contested. A 2015 report on proposed FEMA changes said many of the changes involved Canary Ditch, which runs through the north and west sides of the city, and that about 70 percent of Franklin's industrial areas fell in the 100-year flood zone under the proposal. A local insurance agent quoted in the story estimated that homeowners in newly designated areas could need flood coverage costing $1,500 or more a year.

  • Look up the parcel on FEMA's current flood map before you list, since the 2015 maps were proposals at the time of that report.
  • Ask your insurer whether the house has a flood policy and what it costs.
  • If your home was damaged in 2008 or since, gather repair records and permits.

Manufacturing is the main named employer group. Toyota, NSK, KYB and Mitsubishi all have operations in the city, according to Wikipedia. Ritters Frozen Custard started in Franklin and now franchises in other markets, and in the 1910s the Indiana Motor and Manufacturing Company built cars and trucks here.

The city's position on I-65 and U.S. 31, about 20 miles from Indianapolis, puts these employers and the capital region within reach of one address.

sections.h2: What did the flood buyouts change for neighbors near the old flood area?
sections.html:
The buyouts left open ground where houses once stood, so a street near the old flood area may now back onto trees and trails instead of neighbors. The 2014 report said the city had been buying and demolishing flood-damaged homes since 2010, and that trees, trail markers and paths were paid for with resident donations and grants from the Johnson County Community Foundation.

In 2013 the city was finalizing deals to demolish four of the last six homes in the program, and the county was nearing demolition of the final two. If your house is close to a former buyout site, tell a buyer what you know about its history and show any elevation or insurance paperwork. A buyer who hears it from you is less likely to feel it was hidden.

sections.h2: Which schools and transit options serve Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin Community Schools serves almost all of the city, including Franklin Community High School. It runs five in-person elementary schools and the Franklin Community Virtual School for grades 5 to 12. A small northern section of the city falls within the Clark-Pleasant Community School Corporation.

Freight rail runs through town on the Louisville and Indiana Railroad. Franklin Flying Field is about 3.5 miles south of downtown, and Indianapolis International Airport is about 28 miles northwest. Access Johnson County provides bus service.

Because two school corporations touch the city, confirm which one covers a given address before you describe schools to a buyer.

sections.h2: What does a Franklin seller do about taxes and the Sales Disclosure Form?
sections.html:
Every Indiana sale for money needs a Sales Disclosure Form signed by both parties, reviewed by the Johnson County assessor and filed with the county auditor (Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5). The auditor cannot accept the deed without it. A $20 fee applies, with exceptions for transfers such as foreclosure, divorce, probate and condemnation.

Property tax goes to the Johnson County Treasurer, at 86 W. Court Street in the West Annex Building downtown, according to a local news report. That report listed spring taxes due May 10 and fall taxes due November 10, and gave a phone number of 317-346-4330. The state's Department of Local Government Finance lists May 11 and November 10 for 2026, with a 5 percent penalty for a payment within 30 days and 10 percent after that.

  • Payments can be made online, by phone, by mail, in person, in the drop box outside the West Annex Building, or at several local banks.
  • Card payments carry fees, while electronic checks and mailed checks do not.
  • Ask for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

The local news report named First Financial Bank, First Merchants Bank, First National Bank, Horizon Bank and Mutual Savings Bank as branches that accept tax payments with the original coupon. Online card payments carried a 2.5 percent fee, with a $1.50 minimum, and Visa debit carried $3.95 per transaction. Fees change, so check the treasurer's site before you pay.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer, and each path suits a different house and a different calendar.

  • List the house if it is in good repair and you have time for showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Sell privately if you are comfortable handling disclosures and negotiation without an agent.
  • Ask for a cash offer if the house has flood history, deferred repairs, a tenant or an unresolved estate.

We buy houses in Franklin as they are. You can request an offer, compare it to the other routes, and say no if it does not fit.

faqs.q: What county is Franklin, Indiana in?
faqs.a: Franklin is in Johnson County and is the county seat. It is about 20 miles south of Indianapolis on I-65 and U.S. 31.

faqs.q: Was Franklin hit by a flood?
faqs.a: Yes. In June 2008, creeks overflowed and more than 100 houses were damaged or destroyed. The city and county later bought many of the flooded homes.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance to sell a house in Franklin?
faqs.a: Not to sell, but a buyer's lender may require it if the home is in a mapped flood zone. Check the current FEMA flood map for your parcel.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state lists May 11 and November 10 for 2026. Paying within 30 days after the due date adds 5 percent, and later payment adds 10 percent.
Franklin Community Schools serves almost all of the city. A small northern section is in the Clark-Pleasant Community School Corporation.

faqs.q: What paperwork does the county need when a Franklin house sells?
faqs.a: A Sales Disclosure Form signed by seller and buyer, reviewed by the assessor and filed with the auditor. A $20 fee applies unless an exception covers the transfer.
